fundamentals:
React builds on a handful of plain ideas: DOM nodes, function calls that return objects, functions that return those objects, and the browser's own forms. This module peels them back one layer at a time, starting from a product card built by hand with the DOM and ending with lists that keep the right state on the right item. By the end, nothing in React's core API should feel like magic.

Every example comes from one small product store app (examples/product-store in the site's repository). The outputs you see (console logs, HTML, URLs, request bodies, warnings, TypeScript errors) were recorded by running it in Chrome, not written by hand.

Read the notes in order: each one removes one layer of sugar. JSX → createElement → plain objects → DOM is the thread that runs through all of them.
internals:
How React works under the hood, meaning reconciliation, the Fiber architecture, the work loop, the commit phase, scheduling and hooks, at the level a frontend developer needs to reason about their own code. It's not a workshop write-up. The notes are built from react.dev, the React team's own architecture writing, and the React 19.2.5 source (react-dom-client.development.js, scheduler.development.js), which every algorithm here was checked against.

Everything follows one throughline. Your components return elements → React reconciles them against a tree of fibers → it walks that tree in a loop it can pause → it commits the result to the DOM in one go. The optimizations in React Performance and the concurrent features in React Suspense are all consequences of that pipeline.

New to this? Start with React Internals - Start Here: the reading order, a plain-English glossary, and interview-value labels ( must know · good to know · skip).
